title: Inside an async executor
subtitle: Three tasks, one thread: poll, Pending, wake, poll again
captions: Three tasks are spawned. Nothing has run yet: a future is an inert state machine until somebody polls it. All three sit in the ready queue.
The executor polls task A. It runs until its first .await on a socket that has no data, so it returns Poll::Pending. Before returning, the socket future hands its Waker to the reactor.
Same for task B: it runs up to await #1, registers its waker and yields. The thread never blocks inside a task, it moves on.
Task C is polled and also parks on I/O. The ready queue is empty, so the executor thread goes to sleep (in Tokio, inside epoll_wait/kqueue).
Data arrives for B. The reactor calls waker.wake(), which pushes B back onto the ready queue and wakes the executor thread.
B is polled again. The state machine resumes exactly after await #1, runs to await #2 and returns Pending once more.
A's I/O completes: its waker re-queues it. Note that the order of completion is decided by the outside world, not by spawn order.
A resumes from await #1 and suspends at await #2. Its local variables live inside the future itself, not on a thread stack.
Two events at once: C and B are both woken and queued. Waking is cheap: it is just a pointer pushed onto a queue.
C resumes after await #1 and reaches await #2, which is not ready yet: Pending.
B is polled, its last .await is ready, the function returns: Poll::Ready(value). B is finished and its memory is freed.
The remaining I/O completes and A and C are woken together.
C completes. Three concurrent tasks ran on one thread, which was busy only while there was actual work to do.
